dedupe_keys.name: patientflow real time prediction of hospital bed demand from current and incoming patients

description: patientflow is a Python package that predicts how many hospital beds will be needed in the next few hours, from patients already in the emergency department and from patients expected to arrive. The producers are Zella King and colleagues at University College London, who first built it for University College London Hospitals to forecast emergency admissions over an eight-hour window from real-time electronic health record data, and published it in the Journal of Open Source Software in 2025. Coverage: the method was developed and validated at one London hospital trust, but the package is written to take any hospital's patient snapshots. It turns each patient's record at a prediction time into a probability of admission, aggregates these into a probability distribution of bed counts by specialty, adds expected arrivals from past patterns, and evaluates the forecasts. The code is available on GitHub and PyPI under the free MIT licence, with notebooks and a synthetic data set; an anonymised UCLH data set is on Zenodo with restricted access. Caveats: a hospital must extract its own EHR snapshots, the models are statistical, not simulations of physical flow, and results from one trust may not transfer. Simulation uses: short-term bed capacity planning, testing how surges in emergency demand fill beds, and feeding hospital capacity into disaster or heatwave scenarios. Related records: the KHP patient flow simulator (model-khp-patient-flow-simulator) and the SimPy healthcare models (model-simpy-streamlit-healthcare-des) simulate hospital flow as queues.
inputs: Patient snapshots extracted from an electronic health record at set prediction times (location, observations, lab orders and results, consult requests)
Past arrival patterns to the emergency department
Synthetic data set bundled with the repository
